title: Cabbage Cake Stuffed with Spinach and Mushrooms
subtitle: a layered vegan cabbage and rice cake
description: Layers of cabbage leaves and a mushroom, spinach and rice filling are slowly cooked in a pot with a tomato sauce, then turned out as an impressive vegan main.

steps.text: If the cabbage leaves are not already blanched, blanch them in a pot of plenty of boiling water for about 5 minutes. Drain and cool.

Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the chopped mushrooms, spinach and onions until the spinach wilts, the onions are translucent and there is almost no liquid left. Transfer to a bowl and mix in the rice, coriander, baharat, salt and pepper.
Mix the sauce ingredients (finely chopped tomatoes, sliced garlic, oil, paprika, salt and pepper) in a bowl.

Grease a pot with olive oil, place a round of baking paper the size of the pot in the base and pour a quarter of the sauce over it. Lay 2-3 blanched cabbage leaves over the base so the edges hang over the sides and overlap slightly. Spread a layer of the rice mixture on top, then another quarter of the sauce. Cover with 2-3 more cabbage leaves. Repeat until all the filling is used, finishing with a layer of cabbage leaves with no sauce on top. Fold the overhanging leaves over to enclose the cake.
Cover the cake with a plate of suitable size or a round of baking paper so the liquids cook the cake and do not evaporate.
Pour 1/3 cup water over the covered cake, cover the pot and cook over very low heat for 2 hours.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Transfer the covered pot to the oven for 30 minutes.
Remove the lid, pour over 2 tbsp olive oil and bake for about 30 more minutes until the top is golden. Turn the cake out onto a serving plate and serve.
